name: GIMP batch
role: Headless GIMP via --batch with Script-Fu or Python; heavyweight, version-specific procedures
summary: GIMP's non-interactive mode: gimp-console (or gimp -i) with -b/--batch commands and --batch-interpreter selecting Script-Fu (default) or another interpreter, then --quit. Gives access to GIMP's full procedure database, layers and plug-ins from scripts. Script procedures differ between GIMP 2 and 3, so every script is version-specific. Distinguishing strength: reproducing GIMP-only operations without the GUI.
use_when: A GIMP-specific operation (layer modes, plug-in filter, XCF layers) has no CLI equivalent elsewhere
Batch-converting or editing existing .xcf files with layers intact
Reusing an existing Script-Fu routine unchanged
avoid_when: Resize, crop, convert, annotate: ImageMagick starts faster and is the validated baseline
Colour-managed or EXR sequence work: oiiotool
Needing stability across GIMP majors: scripts break between 2.10 and 3
notes: 2026-10-26: The official_url man page documents GIMP 3 (data dir 3.0, config dir 3.2): -b/--batch, --batch-interpreter (default Script-Fu), --quit, -i; GIMP_BATCH_INTERPRETER is legacy and --pdb-compat-mode exists for deprecated procedures. GIMP 2 scripts used different procedure names and python-fu-eval; whether python-fu-eval is registered in GIMP 3 was not verified. Python is not covered on that page.
2026-10-26: Homebrew cask gimp is at 3.2.6 (upstream 2026-09-10); the gimp CLI path inside the macOS app bundle was not verified.

assessment.rationale: GIMP 3.2.6 released 2026-09-10 per gimp.org downloads; man page documents the GIMP 3 batch interface. Valid but heavyweight and version-bound; a niche behind ImageMagick for scripted edits.
